I like this charming film. The whimsical narration captures the mood of a lazy Sunday, not taking itself too seriously. I am trying to reach family members of the late director, Stewart Wilensky, should anyone have contact info.

A laid-back look at the Village of the early '60s. The atmosphere of this slice of New York is captured well. We even hear a beat poet. It's not altogether candid. The story inserts a woman wearing gloves and a striped dress a la Jacquie Kennedy wandering around, looking out of place. Oh, and some dark-haired guy with a guitar. The minimal music arrangement is an excellent choice.

An interesting overview of 1960's New York (more specifically Greenwich Village). This film has the mood down pat, with the banjos, bongos and the hip language of the period. It takes us on a tour of everyday practices then (oh, maybe it hasn't changed) taking us through art exhibitions on the street, men playing bocce (sigh) and other sights. Although pretty much filled with interesting locals, I REALLY with they didn't include the obviously eyesore actors, who stick out like a sore thumb. But other then that, a highly enjoyable film! Reccomended!

rv: I feel compelled to add a great review to push down the one that refers to this film as "trash"... This animated gem was made at the turn of the twentieth century. It features the first animated character with a very real personality. Watch this and imagine your only experiences with cartoons are in the newspaper. Then you see this film, and the cartoon moves! It had to be awe inspiring. Gertie, Nemo, and the other works of Windsor McCay have inspired countless artists, cartoonists, and film makers. We are so fortunate that we live in a time when films such as these are archived and accessible

It was also a time when much of the country had no access to museums of any account, and dinosaurs were something that they might have heard of, but that was about all. It was also a time when P.T.
